skill.name: requesting-code-review
skill.description: Guides agents to request structured code reviews after implementation milestones and before merging changes.
skill.summary: Prompts a dedicated reviewer to compare changes against requirements before merge.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from markdown examples, template placeholders, and code-review guidance. The skill asks users to run read-only git commands for review context and does not contain hidden execution, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Git command examples can be mistaken for executable automation.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that commands are optional, read-only examples, and recommend validating commit references before use.

remediation.issue: The review prompt uses commit placeholders in shell examples.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to paste only trusted commit SHAs or branch names from their own repository.

content.value_statement: Code changes can miss defects when implementation and review happen in the same flow. This skill provides a repeatable review prompt for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Defines when to request review during task work and before merge.
Shows how to collect base and head git references for a review range.
Provides a reusable code-review prompt template for a reviewer agent.
Guides reviewers to compare changes against requirements and tests.
Organizes findings into Critical, Important, and Minor groups.
Asks for a clear merge readiness assessment with reasoning.
limitations: It does not run tests or inspect code by itself.
It depends on accurate base and head commit references.
It cannot guarantee that every defect will be found.
It assumes the reviewer has access to the relevant repository context.

use_cases.title: Review a Completed Feature
use_cases.description: Request a structured review after implementing a feature and before starting the next task.

use_cases.title: Check Merge Readiness
use_cases.description: Compare a git diff against requirements before merging changes into the main branch.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Add regular review checkpoints to subagent-driven development so issues are fixed earlier.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after finishing a small task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my recent change for correctness, tests, and merge readiness. Focus on defects that should be fixed before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Requirement Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a change must match a written plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the implementation against these requirements. Identify missing behavior, test gaps, and any important risks before merge.

prompt_templates.title: Git Range Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when base and head commits are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changes between my base and head commits. Categorize findings as Critical, Important, or Minor, and give a merge verdict.

prompt_templates.title: Production Readiness Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before shipping a significant feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature for production readiness. Check architecture, edge cases, migrations, compatibility, security concerns, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for review after adding verification and repair functions.
output: Strengths: The reviewer notes clear architecture and meaningful tests.
Important issue: Missing progress feedback during long operations should be fixed.
Assessment: Ready to proceed after the important issue is addressed.

output_examples.input: A maintainer requests review before merging a command-line change.
output: Strengths: The implementation matches the requested workflow.
Important issue: Help text is incomplete, so users may miss new options.
Assessment: Merge with fixes after documentation and help output are updated.

best_practices: Request review after each substantial task or before merging to the main branch.
Provide the reviewer with requirements, a concise description, and the relevant git range.
Fix Critical and Important findings before continuing with dependent work.
anti_patterns: Skipping review because a change appears simple.
Treating every minor style comment as a release blocker.
Ignoring valid technical feedback without evidence from code or tests.

faq.question: Does this skill perform the code review automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and a prompt template for requesting a focused review from another agent.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does the skill ask for base and head commits?
faq.answer: They define the exact change range so the reviewer can inspect the intended diff.

faq.question: Should Critical findings block progress?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends fixing Critical findings immediately before continuing.

faq.question: Can I challenge a reviewer finding?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends pushing back with technical reasoning and supporting tests when the reviewer is wrong.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for human review?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure AI-assisted review, but teams should keep required human review policies.
